source_text: Iam reliqua, licet aliquibus sermonibus variata, contexuit. Contra has ergo obiectiones meas nihil quo repercuterer excogitavit; sed verum me collegisse, argumentandi inopia confessus, dicit mihi ad haec omnia Apostolum respondere debere, qui pronuntiet, per unum hominem peccatum intrasse in hunc mundum. In quo loco, quis eum eruditus sanum habuisse caput aestimet, qui non intellexerit aut praetereunda sibi esse, contra quae nihil poterat invenire, aut quaecumque excogitanda, quae referret obiectis, ad quorum confirmationem Apostoli verba coniungeret?
pass_a_gloss: Already the remaining things, although varied by some speeches, he wove together. Against these objections of mine, therefore, he thought out nothing by which I might be struck back; but having confessed by a lack of arguing that I had collected truly, he says to me that the Apostle ought to answer to all these things, who pronounces that through one human being sin entered into this world. In which place, who of the learned would estimate that he had a sound head, who did not understand that either those things against which he could find nothing ought to be passed by, or whatever things ought to be thought out which he might bring back to the things objected, for whose confirmation he would join the Apostle's words?

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS relative; Rom 5:12 in quo omnes peccaverunt — keep Latin force

pass_b_english: He then assembled the rest, although varying some expressions. Against these objections of mine he devised nothing that could strike back at me. Confessing through his lack of an argument that my conclusion was true, he says that the apostle must answer all these points for him—the apostle who declares that sin entered this world through one man (Romans 5:12). At this point, what educated person could think him sound in the head? He did not understand that he should either pass over objections against which he could find nothing, or think up some answer to them and attach the apostle’s words in support of it.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
